ruled in its final form by the advisor's 2026-10-14 review, PART 2, after the rule's first form failed the recorded-correct regression vector 102-Q1): the stage-1 reading's recognition classes and the headline rule the advisor ruled, verbatim: 'A derivation input is not a stated result. In the last results section that attributes the item's quantity, a quantity that is an operand of arithmetic the answer shows is attributed to no item. An operand is a number standing on either side of a binary operator: *, +, a spaced -, or ^ followed by a digit, sign or bracket. A slash divides between bare numbers written without spaces (210/17), or between quantities of different known dimensions (12.0 V / 6.00 k ohm). A slash between quantities of the same dimension, or where one side carries no unit, lists them (61.8 MPa / 176 MPa, 12.35 / 17.65 kN), and they stay stated values. The value an equation produces - the member after its last '=' - is stated unless an operator touches it. The degree sign's normalised '^ deg' is not an exponent, and an unspaced hyphen between numbers is a range, not a minus. Every other quantity is collected as before, under the unchanged attribution guards, and the item fails when any collected quantity lies outside the frozen key's tolerance.' Amendment, 2026-10-14: '=' is not an operator. A clause ends at ';', at a comma or full stop followed by a space, or at the end of the line, and its members are the parts between its '=' signs. A member before the clause's last '=' is arithmetic when it contains an operator, and every quantity in it is an operand. A member with no operator is a stated value, however many '=' follow it: '12.4 kN = 12 352.9 N' states both. A lowercase x with a space on each side multiplies, like * and ×. A ^ inside a unit (mm^2) belongs to the unit and is not an operator. The amendment repairs the implementation's positional reading of the ruling's last-member sentence - the guarded form read every member before a line's last '=' as a derivation input, whatever it held, which goes past the ruling and brings back the order-dependence the rule exists to remove ('Aluminum force = 12.4 kN = 12 352.9 N' passed while the order-swapped 'Aluminum force = 12 352.9 N = 12.4 kN' failed, and 'Aluminum force = 13.0 kN = 12 352.9 N' passed on a wrong figure): under the amendment a no-operator member states its figures, so both orders fail the item and the wrong figure fails it. - under the attribution guards (a token distinctive to the item - its own tokens minus its same-dimension siblings' - and no token distinctive to a rival, function words never attributing, headings as section delimiters, parenthesized asides, LaTeX digit grouping and inline-math delimiters normalized away, and bound words introducing requirements rather than values); the stage-1 reading's five false positives now fail and its eighteen false negatives now pass, the 58 sampled entries re-scored under frozen-2026-10-03.3 agreeing with the advisor's resolution 58/58 (stage 1 itself stays reported under frozen-2026-10-03.2, with the side-by-side re-score of all 105 units committed with the repair), and K1, the Q23 key's mixed significant-figure tolerance, is the owner's next key version - keys.json is untouched. The operand guard the ruling adds - the repair of the first form's 102-Q1 failure - moves, across the run's 71 delivered answers, exactly one item on one unit (C-Q23-r2's Common extension, FAIL to PASS, 2/5 to 3/5 items, the verdict unchanged FAIL: the '3/3400 m = 8.8235×10⁻⁴ m' derivation the extension's results table shows, whose slash operands the unguarded rule collected as stated quantities, the 3400 m far outside the 0.882353 mm key), so the review's stop condition - any move beyond that item - is not met. The 2026-10-14 clause amendment moves nothing on the run's 71 delivered answers against the guarded form it amends - 0 verdicts, 0 item counts and 0 items move, and the advisor's own probe measured 0 - so the guarded form's measurements hold under it unchanged. Ruled against the committed first form, the rule moves two units' item readings, both inside Q23: C-Q23-r3, PASS 5/5 to FAIL 3/5 - the final-conclusion table's rounded force figures (12.4 and 17.6 kN) are stated values outside the keys' tolerances (12.35 and 17.65 kN) - and E-Q23-r2, verdict unchanged FAIL, 3/5 to 1/5 - both tensile-stress items flip on the answer's kill-trigger limits ('below 93 MPa' and '< 265 MPa'): a comparison is not an operator, so the limit figures stay stated values, and both lie far outside the stress keys (61.8 and 176.5 MPa); whether a kill-trigger limit should attribute to the item it bounds is a verdict-semantics question for the advisor's ruling, reported as it reads (convention 18). plan.stage: stage 1 of the staged plan (the owner's 2026-10-05 directive: tier 3 runs in stages; the stage-2 rule is pre-registered under execution)
plan.unit: one (question, repetition, arm) triple: one question from the frozen questions.json, one of its three repetitions, answered under one arm's registered treatment, scored once by the frozen scorer
plan.question_source: evals/tier2/questions.json (the model-visible file: id, shape, domain, question). Every arm receives exactly this text; no arm receives keys.json, the model answers, or the wrong answers.

question_selection.rule: Fixed by rule before any run (the owner's 2026-10-05 directive, specification 1): draw from Q6-Q25 only. Q1-Q5 are calibration-exposed - the 2026-10-03/04 golden probes answered them under the pre-freeze configuration - and are reserved for stage 2, where they are reported separately as calibration-exposed. Take one question per shape (five questions: the five shapes the frozen set carries), then two more questions from two different shapes, so exactly two shapes contribute a second question and the other three contribute one each.
question_selection.algorithm: random.Random(SELECTION_SEED) over the frozen set's Q6-Q25, questions in frozen-set order. Step 1 - one per shape: for each of the five shapes in the order the shapes first appear in the frozen set, random.choice over that shape's Q6-Q25 questions. Step 2 - two more from two different shapes: random.sample over the five shape names (first-appearance order) for the two shapes, then for each named shape random.choice over that shape's questions not already selected. The seven ids are recorded below in frozen-set order.
question_selection.coverage: all five shapes; SANITY and PROCEDURE each contribute a second question
question_selection.guard: The guard test (tests/test_tier3_manifest.py) reconstructs the selection from this rule and this seed independently of the runner's own implementation, and fails under a different seed.
question_selection.stage_2_remainder_note: The remaining 18 questions of the frozen set: Q1-Q5 (calibration-exposed, reported separately) and the 13 Q6-Q25 questions the selection did not take (Q7, Q8, Q9, Q11, Q12, Q13, Q18, Q19, Q20, Q21, Q22, Q24, Q25).

A.name: inexpensive-single-call
A.treatment: One model call, the request only. No tools, no workflow, no retrieval. The serving is the experiment's inexpensive reference.
A.model_selection_criterion: The harness's triage-tier serving: the cheapest tier the harness uses productively, measured to classify reliably when pinned (HANDOVER.md section 6, the triage-reliability measurement; the standing triage pin's evidence). Proposed in conversation 2026-10-03; the owner ratifies the pin value in .env.tier3 (env-prefixed, git-ignored).

B.name: same-model-with-tools
B.treatment: The same serving as arm A (the same pin value by design - the two arms differ only in the registered tool treatment), with two deterministic tools: primary-source acquisition and recomputation. The prompt is arm A's prompt with exactly two differences and no others: the first paragraph names the tools ('Use the tools registered below where they help', where arm A's says 'Answer from your own knowledge...'), and the tool registration sits between the answer format and the closing 'Answer now.' Replacing arm B's first paragraph with arm A's and removing the tool section yields arm A's prompt exactly - the property the manifest test checks mechanically (the earlier draft, which kept arm A's 'no tools are available' paragraph while registering tools, was self-contradictory; the old test enforced the contradiction, and tier3-2 corrects both). The question text, the deadline and the scoring are identical.
B.model_selection_criterion: Identical to arm A's pin value - the arm exists to isolate the tool treatment, so the two pins must resolve to the same serving. The owner sets both to the same value.
B.call_structure: Calls 1 and 2 offer the tools; call 3 keeps them declared with tool_choice "none" (the model sees the tools it may not use, and answers). At most 3 model calls and 20 tool invocations per unit. Every invocation is recorded: the tool, its arguments, the result's size, any error. A tool failure is recorded and the model continues without the tool; the delivered answer is scored on what it delivered.

tools.fetch_primary_source: Fetches the archived July 1, 2014 text of the CFR section a question cites, written as the question writes it (for example '29 CFR § 1910.146(b)'). Closed-world: the world is the committed archive under evals/tier2/sources/ (the archived sections the lookup questions cite); any other citation returns a typed not-available result, which is a result, not a failure. Opens no network connection.
tools.recompute: Evaluates one arithmetic expression and returns its value: numbers, the four operations and powers, parentheses, pi and e, and the functions sqrt, exp, ln, log10, sin, cos, tan, their inverses, abs, min and max. The expression is parsed and walked as a syntax tree - it is never evaluated, executed or compiled as code (hard rule 3); anything outside that grammar, an exponent beyond 1000, or a result beyond 1e300 is a typed rejection. No model judgment, no external calls.

B.ceiling_note: Raised from $0.20 by tier3-4 (the owner's 2026-10-05 directive, specification 4): the tool loop's third call carries the accumulated tool results, and the measured plan-scale units (the 2026-10-04 probes) showed a large plan can spend the old ceiling's headroom on one call.

C.name: complementary-model-cooperation
C.treatment: Two servings with complementary measured strengths cooperate under a fixed protocol: model 1 drafts, model 2 independently checks, model 1 revises once if model 2 objects. The protocol, not the models' own discretion, decides what is delivered.
C.model_selection_criterion: Complementary pair measured in this repository's lab notebook: the engineering-tier serving (measured to converge the build loop - HANDOVER.md sections 6.9 and 6.11) and the escalation-tier serving (measured to hold escalation 19/20 against 13/20 in the 086 escalation shootout, docs/traces/086-escalation-shootout.jsonl - a shootout that graded escalation output, not direct answers to questions). Complementary, not equivalent: one is measured on engineering convergence, the other on escalation judgment. Proposed in conversation 2026-10-03; the owner ratifies both pin values in .env.tier3.
C.check: Model 2's check returns a typed verdict, not prose: a JSON object {"concur": boolean, "objections": [string]}, concur true exactly when objections is empty. The runner parses the verdict (control flow never reads prose - hard rule 2); a reply that is not a valid verdict is retried within the bound (2 attempts), and a check that returns no valid verdict after the bounded retries is recorded as unavailable - never as concurrence - and model 1's draft is delivered. The three calls are a hard whole-sequence bound: the check's bounded retries compete with the revision for the third call, so a revision runs only when the check objected AND a call remains; the starvation path is recorded, not hidden.
C.disagreement_handling: Model 2's objections are recorded in the run transcript (the typed verdict's objections list). The delivered answer is model 1's revised answer when model 2 objected (one revision round), or model 1's draft when model 2 concurred. There is no voting and no third model.
C.ceiling_note: Raised from $0.20 by tier3-4 (the owner's 2026-10-05 directive, specification 4): the pair's three calls carry the draft and the objection list, and the measured plan-scale units showed a large plan can spend the old ceiling's headroom on one call.

D.name: stronger-single-call
D.treatment: One model call, the request only - arm A's shape with a stronger serving. The strong reference arm: the experiment's comparison point for whether the inexpensive arms' gap is a serving gap or a treatment gap.
D.model_selection_criterion: The strongest single serving measured in this repository: the escalation-tier serving that held escalation 19/20 against 13/20 in the 086 escalation shootout (docs/traces/086-escalation-shootout.jsonl - a shootout that graded escalation output, not direct answers to questions), the strongest measured hold rate in the lab notebook. Proposed in conversation 2026-10-03; the owner ratifies the pin value in .env.tier3.
D.prompt: prompts/arm_d.md (identical to arm A's prompt - the same request, only the serving differs)

E.name: current-pipeline
E.treatment: The current pipeline: the question enters as a request through the full harness workflow (the graph engine, workflows/*.yaml, triage and engineering phases, escalation as routed), under the standing pins in .env, with the common deadline as its timeout so the harness's own watchdog ends the run by its own terminal. Delivered means the pipeline's completed terminal: the terminal phase's conclusion (verdicts.implement.summary), read the way the record reads it. A judge-approved draft that no completed terminal shipped is scored and reported beside the delivered count as 'approved, not shipped' - never counted as delivered (Ruling D50 (3)). A run that ended without an answer is an incomplete unit.
E.model_pin_env: the standing pins (.env, the owner's) - no experiment pin
E.model_selection_criterion: The owner's standing configuration, unchanged. Arm E exists so the experiment compares against what the harness ships today.
E.tool_invocations: the pipeline's own (research, grounding) under its standing risk gates
E.prompt: prompts/arm_e.md (the question as the harness's scenario request - the pipeline's own entry point)

interleaved_order.algorithm: Enumerate the 105 stage-1 units as (question_id, repetition, arm) with question_id in the frozen questions.json order over the seven selected questions (the plan's question_selection), repetition in 1..3, arm in A,B,C,D,E; then random.Random(20261003).shuffle(the list). Units execute in the shuffled order - no arm runs as a block, so time-of-day and serving-load confounds distribute across arms. The order seed is the experiment's own (the same registration the 375-unit tier3-3 plan carried: the seed is the recorded constant, the enumeration is the plan's).
interleaved_order.reproducibility: The seed is recorded here; the order is reconstructable exactly. The runner records the seed and the resulting order's sha256 in the results header, and the guard test reconstructs the order independently and checks the two digests match.

execution.deadline_note: One wall-clock deadline for every unit of every arm, enforced by the runner's watchdog. A unit that exceeds it is stopped and recorded as a deadline failure. Raised from 600 to 1800 seconds by tier3-4 (the owner's 2026-10-05 directive and the advisor's ruling of the same date): the measured engineering pace (the 2026-10-04 probes, 161.435 s per feasibility node against a 312.8-365.5 s plan node) showed a plan-scale unit cannot fit 600 s before any judging round. The scenario YAMLs' own timeouts are the golden pass rule (twice each question's time target), versioned under D44, and are not edited - probes use copies with the probe's deadline; tier 3's deadline changes only through the manifest, as tier3-4.
execution.isolation: Every unit executes inside _isolated_store() (autornd.evals.runner): a fresh temporary knowledge store per question-run, no cross-run memory. This is the per-question-run instantiation of the command's 'isolated stores per question-run; no cross-run memory'.
execution.retry_rules: Transient provider failures (empty replies, 429, 5xx) are retried by the harness's existing retry policy, bounded, with backoff. A unit that exhausts its retries is an incomplete run: delivered correctness 0, its cost and latency recorded and counted. Retries are recorded per unit with their attribution (the runner's retries record).
execution.spend_enforcement: Each unit's client carries its arm's per-question-run ceiling (the runner's spend_ceiling); the whole experiment runs under a SweepBudget whose cap is the owner's ratified total authorization (the fit rule composes the two ceilings: a unit starts only if it could not overrun the sweep cap). The sweep cap is the authorization ceiling, not a prediction. For stage 1 the per-unit ceilings compose to $37.80 (21 units per arm at $0.10/$0.50/$0.50/$0.20/$0.50); the owner's ratified amount, authorized 2026-10-05, is $30.00, and the manifest carries the owner's ratified amount (the owner's instruction: where the runner requires TIER3_SPEND_AUTHORIZED to equal a manifest figure, the manifest carries the owner's ratified amount instead). The owner may authorize a lower TIER3_SPEND_AUTHORIZED and the sweep's fit rule then applies: a unit the fit rule does not start is recorded as not started (the runner's skipped status, its stop reason on the record), never silently dropped - the success measures' denominators are the 21 planned units per arm, the not-started included.
execution.information_access: Equal across arms except the registered treatments: the same question text (read from the frozen questions.json), the same deadline, the same seeded order, the same scorer, the same isolation. The only differences are the registered treatments - the serving(s), the tools, the cooperation protocol, and the pipeline itself.
execution.no_model_access_to_keys: keys.json is read only by the scorer process after each unit's answer is delivered. No arm's prompt, tool, or workflow returns key material. The fetch tool's closed world is the committed archive under evals/tier2/sources/, not the keys.

registered_call_parameters.finish_reason: recorded per call; a truncated answer (finish_reason=length) is scored as delivered and flagged (the unit record's truncated field)
registered_call_parameters.note: Every parameter a unit's outcome depends on is registered here rather than buried in a call site. Arms A-D's calls carry these max_tokens and temperature; arm E's calls carry the pipeline's own standing caps (the .env tier caps), which the preflight checks against the pinned endpoints' max_completion_tokens.

execution.resolved_servings_recorded: Every unit's record names the pin that served it, resolved from the environment at run time, and every call's resolved model and provider is on the client's accounting record (the unit record's providers_by_tier).
execution.resume: The results log is append-only (one JSONL line per unit, flushed as written, with a durable mirror outside the repo). A restart with the same manifest version and order digest skips every unit already recorded - nothing runs twice or out of order. The unit in flight at the interruption (a unit_started line with no unit record) is charged its full per-unit ceiling against the sweep as unreconciled liability, then re-run. A restart with a different manifest version or order digest refuses.
execution.record: One JSONL line per unit (the runner's ResultsLog unit record): the arm, the question id, the repetition, the pin that served (resolved from the environment at run time), the delivered answer, the scorer's per-item results and verdict, calls, seconds, cost, cost by tier, providers by tier, retries, refusals, the stop reason, the watchdog, and the unreconciled liability. The header carries the configuration: the seed, the order's sha256, the resolved pin names, the ceilings, and the versions.
execution.stage_2_rule: Pre-registered 2026-10-05, before the first paid unit of stage 1 (the owner's 2026-10-05 directive, specification 3). After stage 1 completes: if arm E's delivered correctness differs from arm A's by 7 or more of the 21 units (|E - A| >= 7/21), the pipeline question is answered, and stage 2 is the owner's option. Otherwise stage 2 runs the remaining 18 questions of the frozen set under this same manifest (the plan's stage_2_remainder: Q1-Q5 plus the 13 unselected Q6-Q25 questions), with Q1-Q5 reported separately as calibration-exposed (the 2026-10-03/04 golden probes answered them under the pre-freeze configuration). The rule is fixed before the first paid unit; it is not adjusted after stage 1's results are known.
execution.stage_2_rule_change_2026_10_05: The advisor's 2026-10-05 review struck one clause from this rule, before any paid unit: 'the difference is large enough that the pipeline's serving, not its treatment, is the measurable cause'. Arms E and A differ in both serving and treatment, and separating the two is what the A-vs-D comparison is for - the rule is a stopping rule only, and names no cause. The rule's decision content is unchanged: the threshold (7 of 21), the owner's-option branch, and the otherwise-branch are exactly as registered.

pilot.authorization: TIER3_PILOT_AUTHORIZED, $7.50 (25 units at $0.10 and 25 at $0.20) - a separate gate from the main run's, so the pilot can be authorized and run alone
pilot.purpose: Calibration: the inexpensive arm against the strong reference on the frozen set, at 1/6 the main run's cost, before the owner decides whether the full authorization is money well spent.
pilot.supersession: Superseded in role by stage 1 (the owner's 2026-10-05 directive): the staged plan's first stage is itself the calibration stage - 7 questions x 3 repetitions x all five arms, 105 units under the owner's $30.00 authorization - so the pilot's question (whether the inexpensive arm against the strong reference is worth the full spend) is answered by stage 1 before any stage-2 spend. The pilot's registration, its gate and its $7.50 authorization are unchanged; whether the pilot mode is deleted from the manifest and the runner is the advisor's ruling, recorded as a question in the 119 response.

preflight.when: Free, before the first unit, after the ratification gates. Its only network call is the catalogue GET itself (unauthenticated, free).
refuses: The worst case of any of arms A-D over its whole call sequence exceeds the arm's per-unit ceiling (the guard's own formula: (prompt bytes + the 512-byte chat-template allowance) x the prompt rate + max_tokens x the completion rate, at the registered max_tokens and the largest prompt the call can carry, arm B's largest archived tool result included; arm C's largest call carries model 1's draft).

Arm B's serving does not list tool support or tool_choice support - R2's final call keeps the tools declared with tool_choice "none", so an endpoint that cannot take tool_choice would fail the call the treatment depends on (the catalogue is blind about supported_parameters: reported, not guessed).

Arm B's context window cannot hold the largest prompt (the registered question, the arm B prompt and the largest archived source, bounded in bytes - D45 amendment (b): a byte-level tokenizer never emits more tokens than bytes) plus the registered max_tokens.

Any serving the lineup names - arm E's included - has no catalogue price the guard can bound (D49: an unknown price is not free - a serving absent from the catalogue, or one carrying a charge beside prompt and completion tokens, is unboundable, and the guard is blind for it).

The registered max_tokens (8000) exceeds a pinned endpoint's max_completion_tokens in the catalogue (the client does not clamp, so the call would fail at the provider). Arm E's tiers are reported, not refused: arm E runs under the guard as it ships.
reports: The catalogue is blind about a serving's supported_parameters, context length or max_completion_tokens.
Arm E's standing tier caps exceed the pinned endpoint's max_completion_tokens.

The arm-E worst-case table (the owner's addition): the worst case per call for each arm E tier under the ratified lineup and the standing caps, against the $0.50 per-unit ceiling, with the guard's formula and the catalogue's rates - saying which calls the guard would refuse and at what spend.

dry_run.what: A mocked run of the full machinery - the gates, the preflight, the plan and its order, the arm executors under their registered treatments and bounds, the deadline, the scoring, the append-only record, the resume, the measures - over the 105-unit stage-1 plan (the seven selected questions, three repetitions, five arms), with the model-serving layer mocked: a scripted client for arms A-D that bills through the real guard and accounting, a fixture catalogue, and a stand-in at the pipeline boundary for arm E (the pipeline's own execution is proven by the harness's suite; everything above the boundary is the experiment's machinery and runs for real). No network, no spend.
dry_run.failure_classes: Each failure class the manifest names, included at least once: refusal, serving_error, deadline, tool failure, an invalid arm C verdict (prose twice - recorded unavailable, never as concurrence), an incomplete unit (a provider failure), and a resume after a kill (the main run is killed after 40 units, the in-flight unit charged its ceiling as unreconciled liability, and the run resumed to the end). The order's sha256 is the guard's reconstruction.
dry_run.pilot_dry_run: The 50-unit pilot, mocked the same way.

reading_sheet.what: Every FAIL unit and a seeded sample of 10 PASS units per arm (seeded order, no arm label), for the two independent hand readings that are the primary measure (Ruling D50 (1)). The merge records agreements, disagreements and unread entries; the five measures are computed scorer-only and again with the readers' verdicts where they read, and the two are reported side by side.

failure_treatment.refusal: A serving that refuses the request delivers nothing: the unit scores 0 and is recorded with the refusal. A unit whose lookups were all refused (arm B's fetch tool) is a poisoned reading, not a model measurement - recorded as such beside the score, the way the runner's refusal line already reports it.
failure_treatment.serving_error: An empty reply with finish "error" is the serving's own failure, never a refusal: the provider failed the call (the stage-1 run's 13 arm-B final-call errors carried finish "error" and 0 tokens - the model never answered). The unit scores 0 and is recorded in its own class, beside and never inside the refusal count.
failure_treatment.timeout: The common deadline. A unit stopped by the watchdog is a deadline failure: 0 delivered, cost and latency recorded and counted.
failure_treatment.tool_failure: Arm B: a tool failure is recorded with the failure (the tool, its arguments, the result's size, any error); the model continues without the tool and the delivered answer is scored on what it delivered. If the run cannot conclude, the unit is incomplete.
failure_treatment.incomplete_runs: Counted in the denominator. The success measures are fractions of the 21 PLANNED units per arm, so an incomplete, refused, timed-out or not-started unit is 0 delivered, never dropped.
failure_treatment.outstanding_liability: Calls that failed after dispatch (the runner's unreconciled_liability, Ruling D45) are recorded per unit and included in that unit's cost and in the total-cost success measure. What a run is on the hook for is part of what it cost to start.

success_measures.delivered_correctness_per_arm: The count of the 21 planned units per arm whose delivered answer the frozen scorer scores PASS, reported as a fraction of 21. This replaces '20 shipped questions means success'.
success_measures.per_question_repeat_outcomes: For each question and arm, the number of its three repetitions that delivered correct: the 0/3, 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 distribution, per arm. Repeatability is itself a measurement - an arm that answers correctly once and wrongly twice is not the arm that answers correctly three times.
success_measures.paired_wins_and_losses_against_A: Paired by question: for each of the 7 selected questions, arm X wins against A when X's correct-repetition count (0-3) exceeds A's, loses when it is lower, ties when equal. Reported as wins/losses/ties per non-A arm across the 7 questions.
success_measures.comparison_with_D: The same paired measure against D (the strong reference). The A-vs-D gap bounds what the treatments can possibly recover; an arm that beats A but not D is a treatment effect inside the inexpensive band, not a serving effect.
success_measures.total_cost_and_latency_including_failure: The sum of cost across all 105 units including refused, timed-out, incomplete, not-started and failed units, with the unreconciled liability included; and latency (total wall-clock and per-unit distribution), likewise including failures. No measure excludes the units that failed.

ratification_gates.gate_1_servings: The owner ratifies every arm's serving - arm E's per tier - by setting TIER3_ARM_A, TIER3_ARM_B, TIER3_ARM_C_1, TIER3_ARM_C_2 and TIER3_ARM_D in .env.tier3 (arm E uses the standing pins, unchanged, and the gate covers them: the resolved map includes arm E's seven tiers). The runner resolves the map, prints it with a fingerprint (the first 12 hex of the sha256 of its canonical JSON), and refuses to start unless TIER3_SERVINGS_RATIFIED equals that fingerprint and TIER3_ARM_B equals TIER3_ARM_A. Until this gate is cleared, no unit starts.
ratification_gates.gate_2_spend: The owner authorizes the stage-1 spend: the owner's ratified amount, $30.00 (authorized 2026-10-05), against the stage-1 compositional ceiling of $37.80 (the 105 planned question-runs: 21 units per arm at $0.10/$0.50/$0.50/$0.20/$0.50) - or $7.50 for the pilot alone (TIER3_PILOT_AUTHORIZED). The $30.00 and the $37.80 are authorization figures, not predicted costs; they are not approved by this manifest. The owner may authorize a lower TIER3_SPEND_AUTHORIZED and the sweep's fit rule then applies (a unit the fit rule does not start is recorded as not started, never silently dropped). Until this gate is cleared, no unit starts.
ratification_gates.stop: STOP before paid execution. The experiment does not start without both gates cleared in one line each by the owner. The runner mechanizes the stop: it refuses to start unless the environment shows both gates cleared (TIER3_SERVINGS_RATIFIED set to the resolved map's fingerprint, and TIER3_SPEND_AUTHORIZED - or TIER3_PILOT_AUTHORIZED for the pilot - set to at least the ratified dollar amount), and it prints the servings map and each missing gate before any network call.

not_prepared_here.paid_execution: The stage-1 main run (105 units, the owner's $30.00 ratified authorization against the $37.80 compositional ceiling) and the pilot (50 units, $7.50) are paid execution: they start only when the owner's ratification gates are cleared. Stage 2, if the stage-2 rule's otherwise-branch fires and the owner opts in, runs the remaining 18 questions under this same manifest. Everything else - the runner (evals/tier3/runner.py), the dry run, the preflight, the worst-case table, the reading sheet, and the tests - is free work, and is done (ARCH-20261003-119; the staged plan registered by the owner's 2026-10-05 directive).

remeasurement.design_record: docs/reviews/2026-10-10-d51-the-request-is-the-yardstick.md (Ruling D51's design record: the plan is its section 8, the predictions its section 9, the decision table its section 7)

A.treatment: One model call, the request only. No tools, no workflow, no retrieval. The serving is the experiment's inexpensive reference (the stage-1 arm A, unchanged).
A.questions: all 25 of the frozen set (Q1-Q25), 3 repetitions each; Q1-Q5 reported separately as calibration-exposed

F.model_pin_env: the standing pins (.env, the owner's) - no experiment pin

E'.name: the-pipeline-under-d51
E'.treatment: Arm E unchanged: the question enters as a request through the standing workflow (workflows/engineering-rnd.yaml - D51's engineering-rnd, after #176) under the standing pins, with the common deadline as its timeout so the harness's own watchdog ends the run by its own terminal. The runner's record label for this arm is 'E'.

E'.tool_invocations: the pipeline's own (research, grounding) under its standing risk gates
E'.questions: stage 1's seven: Q6, Q10, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q17, Q23, 3 repetitions each

units.unit: one (question, repetition, arm) triple: one question from the frozen questions.json, one of its three repetitions, answered under one arm's registered treatment, scored once by the frozen scorer

questions.source: evals/tier2/questions.json (the frozen set, frozen-2026-10-03). Every arm receives exactly this text; no arm receives keys.json, the model answers, or the wrong answers.
questions.a_d_f: all 25 (Q1-Q25), with Q1-Q5 reported separately as calibration-exposed (the 2026-10-03/04 golden probes answered them under the pre-freeze configuration)

order.algorithm: Enumerate the 246 units as (question_id, repetition, arm): A, D and F over the frozen set's 25 questions in frozen-set order, repetition in 1..3, arm in A, D, F; then E' over the seven selected questions in frozen-set order, repetition in 1..3. Then random.Random(20261014).shuffle over the list. Units execute in the shuffled order - no arm runs as a block, so time-of-day and serving-load confounds distribute across arms.
order.reproducibility: The seed is recorded here; the order is reconstructable exactly. The runner records the seed and the resulting order's sha256 in the results header, and the guard test reconstructs the order independently and checks the two digests match.

remeasurement.deadline_note: One wall-clock deadline for every unit of every arm, enforced by the runner's watchdog - unchanged from stage 1.

authorization.note: The $15.00 is an authorization ceiling, not a predicted cost; the plan's expected cost is about $8 (the D51 record's section 8, from stage 1's medians with E' assumed at about $0.15 per unit). The owner may authorize a lower TIER3_SPEND_AUTHORIZED and the sweep's fit rule then applies: a unit the fit rule does not start is recorded as not started, never silently dropped - the success measures' denominators are the 246 planned units, the not-started included. No paid unit starts before the owner has set TIER3_SPEND_AUTHORIZED=15.00 in .env.tier3 (G-3: the owner's file).

scorer.version: frozen-2026-10-03.3 (the scorer on main when the run starts; #171's clause amendment landed on main 2026-10-15)
scorer.k1: K1, the Q23 key's mixed significant-figure tolerance, is not ruled: the report carries key-strict as the primary figure and 3 s.f. side by side, as stage 1 did. The 3 s.f. column re-scores Q23's two force items (12.35 and 17.65 kN at +/-0.01 kN) at +/-0.05 kN - the tolerance that accepts every 3-significant-figure rounding of the key's figures (12.3/12.4 and 17.6/17.7 kN); every other item scores identically under both columns.

reading.rule: The reading sheet holds every scorer FAIL and a seeded sample of 10 PASS units per arm (seeded order, no arm label). Two independent readings under Ruling D50: the advisor's is reading 1, the executor's is reading 2. The executor commits reading 2 before opening the advisor's reading 1.

pre_registration.committed: 2026-10-15, before any paid unit of this run; never edited afterwards (convention 7: each prediction is reported as it reads)
pre_registration.predictions_section_9:
## 9. Predictions

Committed before 120 is built. Each is reported as it reads, never adjusted afterwards (convention 7).

1. **E′ holds at least 14 of 21** key-strict answers on stage 1's seven questions (stage 1: 0). With 3 s.f. accepted (K1), at least 16. Its remaining losses will be mostly Q23 under the strict key, because the engineering serving rounds to 3 s.f. (arm C lost all three Q23 units that way). The rest will show in the record as anchored dissents that escalation overrules.
2. **E′'s median unit costs at most $0.15 and takes at most 400 s** (stage 1: $0.371 and 911 s).
3. **No E′ or F record shows a block, failure or loop iteration caused by a judgment with no anchor.** Any instance is an implementation defect, not a finding.
4. **F is at least A − 1 on the seven questions under both key versions, and at least A − 2 on all 25** (key-strict).
5. **F omits Q15's zeroing step in at most 1 of 3 units** (arm A: 2 of 3).
6. **F's median unit costs at most $0.05,** and at most 5× arm A's median.
7. **If F leaves 5 or more answers unresolved,** those candidates read wrong at a higher rate than F's delivered answers. Below 5, this is reported, not tested.
8. **Agreement predicts correctness (for P5).** On the 25 × 3, a question where all three of an arm's repetitions agree on every asked value is correct more often than one where they disagree.
9. **F's check helps more than it hurts.** Among F units whose check forced a revision, more go from a wrong first answer to a right final answer than from right to wrong. If fewer than 5 units are revised, this is reported, not tested.
pre_registration.decision_table_section_7:
## 7. The sequence

| when | step | owner of the step |
|---|---|---|
| now → about 10-13 | The repair round: #165, #167, #170 rebased; #160, #171 fixed | executor, then advisor review |
| about 10-13 → 10-18 | Command 120: D51 and verify-first, free work | executor, then advisor review by probe |
| about 10-19 → 10-20 | Command 121: the re-measurement's manifest, pre-registration and mocked dry run | advisor writes, executor builds |
| before the run | Spend authorisation; K1 key version or not; pins unchanged | **owner** |
| about 10-21 | The run, overnight | owner launches |
| about 10-22 → 10-24 | Two readings, resolution, verdict, the decision below | advisor and executor |

**After 120 merges, the harness is frozen** until the re-measurement finishes. Only fixes that stop the run from working go in.

**The decision the re-measurement makes:**

| outcome | what it means | next |
|---|---|---|
| Pipeline within 2 of A, verify-first at least A − 1 | The yardstick was the cause, and structure no longer harms. | Verify-first becomes the closed-question candidate default; P3/P4 go into it; the pipeline is tested on tier 4 (P8). |
| Pipeline trails A by 7 or more, verify-first at least A − 1 | The pipeline is not the closed-question lane. | Retire it from closed questions; verify-first is the product there; tier 4 decides the pipeline's fate. |
| Verify-first trails A by 2 or more | Structure still harms closed questions. | Read the anchored dissents; measure each judge's false-fail rate; decide P6 on the escalation rulings. |
| Verify-first beats A | The first evidence that structure adds accuracy here. | Build P3 and P5 into it, and test on harder sets. |
pre_registration.note: The two sections are copied verbatim from the record - the whole of section 9 (the nine predictions) and the whole of section 7 (the sequence and the decision table the re-measurement makes). A test (tests/test_tier3_manifest.py) asserts the sha256 of each copy equals the sha256 of the record's own section, extracted with the record's own section rule; the same copies are pre-registered in docs/handover-review.md section 113, and the test asserts those too.
